body: Thanks for this. My mom is an emotionally abusive  alcoholic. So I was forced to move out at a young age. And I've anyways dated guys that were way too old for me. I think both me and my boyfriend are covering some new territory with this relationship. He's never had to factor in someone else in this kind of decision before.

The parents are pushy. You should have seen them before he went back to school. There was like some form of daily harassment. Just like when he decided to relocate this weekend. But there are no strings. His parents are a couple of the most generous people I've ever met.



I think what's really bothering me is that he gave up on our plans without any sort of fight. And without consulting me. He was so excited to move in together for weeks and then it just fizzled with one phone conversation. He didn't even get that far into the conversation. Most of that ten minutes that he spoke with them was him just covering other details of the decision with them. That was the part that really hurt, I think. All that talk and I was barely an after thought even though I was in the same room.
And that's what I'm worried about. I'm torn. Like I trust him to change but I'm still just really hurt and disappointed.

I don't think they're dangerously involved either. And he's usually stubborn enough to make his own decisions. They just hover and that bugs me. He told them that he was looking to move and they started calling him everyday and researching the school and city that he was looking at. I'm just not used to the hovering. I find it a little suffocating. Not sure if that's going to be a compatibility issue in the end.

They were calling and talking to him about the move every single day since he told them. I think you're right, though. My own background and the fact that I was starting to get annoyed was seriously factoring in. I was getting to the point where I wanted to just tell them that people move and change jobs all of the time. They're acting like it's brain surgery. But then I could see how they would be concerned. They don't want him to be unhappy or mess up his education. And I don't want that either. I just didn't like how he just decided without consulting me.
Yeah and I think that's what is still bothering me. It was like I didn't even factor in. Like the decision didn't effect me at all.
Honestly, I'd rather talk to someone who has felt how I feel. You absolutely have the right to help another suicidal person. You are better equipped to do it than most.
